column1: particularity§The particularity of place names defeats every automatic index.§地名的**特殊性**挫败了所有自动索引。
partisan§Partisan units held the hills for two winters.§**游击队**据守这些山头两个冬天。
partisanship§Partisanship makes every technical question a loyalty test.§**党派之争**把每个技术问题都变成忠诚测试。
passion§The Passion has been performed here every Easter since 1782.§自一七八二年起，每个复活节这里都上演《**受难曲**》。
passivity§Passivity is a choice that looks like an absence of one.§**被动**是一种看起来像没有选择的选择。
pathos§Pathos without restraint becomes sentimentality.§**悲情**若无节制就变成了滥情。
patronage§Political patronage filled the posts long before merit did.§在唯才是举之前，这些职位早已由**政治恩庇**填满。
paucity§There is no paucity of theories, only of tests.§理论从不缺，**缺的是检验**。
pedant§The pedant was right, which is the annoying part.§这个**卖弄学问**的人是对的，恼人的正是这一点。
pedantic§It sounds pedantic until the distinction saves you a lawsuit.§这听起来是在**咬文嚼字**，直到这个区分让你免了一场官司。
pedantry§Pedantry about commas is often laziness about arguments.§在逗号上**斤斤计较**，往往是论证上的懒惰。
peer§He peered into the well and saw nothing at all.§他往井里**窥看**，什么也没看到。
pejorative§The suffix is pejorative and always has been.§这个后缀带**贬义**，一向如此。
penalty§There is a penalty for being early that nobody mentions.§来得太早也有**代价**，只是没人提。
penchant§A penchant for footnotes is an occupational hazard.§**偏爱**脚注是一种职业病。
penitent§The penitent returned the book after eleven years.§这位**忏悔**者在十一年后归还了那本书。
penurious§Penurious with paper, the office was generous with time.§这个办公室在纸张上**吝啬**，在时间上却慷慨。
perceptive§It was perceptive of her to notice what was missing.§她注意到缺了什么，很**有眼力**。
perennial§Perennial plants cost more once and less every year after.§**多年生**植物一次性花费更多，此后每年都更省。
perfectionist§A perfectionist ships nothing and blames the schedule.§**完美主义者**什么都交不出，还怪进度表。
perfidious§Nothing is more perfidious than a friendly review from a rival.§没有什么比来自对手的友善评论更**不可信**。
perfidy§Perfidy on this scale needs at least three people.§这种规模的**背信**至少需要三个人。
perfunctory§A perfunctory thanks is worse than none at all.§**敷衍的**道谢比不谢更糟。
periodic§The periodic table arranges elements by a property nobody could see.§元素**周期**表按一种当时无人看得见的性质排列元素。
periodically§The archive periodically loses a room to another department.§这座档案馆**时不时**就被别的部门占去一个房间。
peripheral§Peripheral vision catches movement the centre misses.§**余光**能捕捉到正视错过的动静。
perishable§Perishable records were copied first and lost anyway.§**易损**的记录被优先抄录，最后还是丢了。
permissive§A permissive grammar describes; a prescriptive one scolds.§**宽容**的语法作描述，规定性的语法则训人。
permutation§There are more permutations than there are seconds in a year.§**排列**组合的数目比一年的秒数还多。
pernicious§The most pernicious errors are the ones that look tidy.§最**有害的**错误是那些看起来很整齐的。
perpetuate§A footnote can perpetuate an error for three centuries.§一条脚注能让一个错误**延续**三个世纪。
perplex§What perplexes me is the confidence, not the conclusion.§让我**困惑**的是那份自信，而不是结论。
perquisite§The perquisites were listed on a card nobody had read.§这些**额外待遇**列在一张没人读过的卡片上。
persevere§Persevere for one more draft; that is usually where it turns.§再**坚持**写一稿，转机通常就在那里。
persist§Persist with a bad method and you will get consistent nonsense.§**坚持**一个坏方法，你会得到前后一致的胡话。
persistent§A persistent low note runs under the whole movement.§一个**持续的**低音贯穿整个乐章。
personality§Personality gets the interview; method keeps the job.§**性格**赢得面试，方法保住工作。
perspicacious§Perspicacious readers wrote in; the rest wrote reviews.§**有洞察力的**读者写信来，其余的写书评。
persuasive§The most persuasive evidence is the evidence you did not need.§最**有说服力的**证据，是你本来不需要的那份。
pertain§The objection pertains to the method and not to the finding.§这个反对意见**针对的是**方法，而不是结论。
pertinent§Keep the pertinent pages and archive the rest.§留下**相关的**几页，其余归档。
perturb§A passing lorry perturbs the instrument for four seconds.§一辆经过的卡车会**干扰**这台仪器四秒钟。
peruse§Perusing does not mean skimming, whatever the usage note says.§不管用法说明怎么讲，peruse 都不是**略读**的意思。
pervasive§A pervasive assumption is the hardest kind to argue with.§**无所不在**的预设是最难反驳的一种。
pestilence§Pestilence, fire and flood are the three headings in the parish book.§教区簿上的三个条目是**瘟疫**、火灾和洪水。
pettiness§Pettiness in an institution is usually a symptom of fear.§一个机构里的**琐碎**计较通常是恐惧的症状。
petulant§A petulant footnote betrays more than a page of argument.§一条**暴躁的**脚注比一页论证泄露得更多。
philanthropic§Philanthropic money comes with a calendar attached.§**慈善**的钱总是附带一份日程表。
phlegmatic§A phlegmatic temperament is an asset in a long project.§**冷静**的性情在长期项目中是资产。
phobic§A phobic response is not persuaded by statistics.§**恐惧症式**的反应不会被统计数字说服。
picayune§Picayune corrections took longer than the substantive ones.§**琐碎**的更正比实质性的更正花的时间还长。
piety§Filial piety and civic duty pulled him in opposite directions.§**孝道**与公民义务把他拉向相反的方向。
pigment§The pigment fades in daylight and the drawings are kept dark.§这种**颜料**在日光下褪色，因此这些素描被存放在暗处。
pilfer§Ideas are pilfered more often than objects and less often noticed.§想法被**顺走**的次数比东西多，被察觉的次数却更少。
pivotal§A pivotal witness changed her account on the third day.§一位**关键**证人在第三天改了口。
placate§He placated the room with a fact and a short silence.§他用一个事实和一段短暂的沉默**安抚**了全场。
placid§A placid temperament is not the same as an incurious one.§**性情平和**并不等于缺乏好奇。
plasticity§Neural plasticity is greatest in the first three years.§神经**可塑性**在头三年最强。
platitude§A platitude is a truth that has stopped doing any work.§**陈词滥调**是一条不再起作用的真理。
plaudit§Plaudits for the design ignored the people who built it.§对设计的**赞誉**忽略了建造它的人。
plausibility§Plausibility is the enemy of verification.§**貌似有理**是核实的敌人。
plausible§Everything he said was plausible and none of it checked out.§他说的一切**听来合理**，却没有一条经得起核对。
playful§A playful footnote is a promise to the reader.§一条**俏皮**的脚注是对读者的一个承诺。
plenitude§A plenitude of sources and a shortage of time.§资料**丰足**，时间却不够。
plentiful§Water is plentiful here and drinkable almost nowhere.§这里**水量充沛**，却几乎没有一处能喝。
plethora§A plethora of committees produced one page of guidance.§**一大堆**委员会最后产出了一页指导意见。
pliant§A pliant assistant is not what a difficult project needs.§一个**逆来顺受**的助手，不是艰难项目所需要的。
plight§He plighted his word and kept it for forty years.§他**许下承诺**，守了四十年。
